round18.ramp_finding: The World Bank Treasury's RAMP does NOT publish its membership. It only counts, and the counts conflict across World Bank pages: 'over 70' (2024 one-pager), '75th member' (April 2024), 'over 80' (May 2025), 'more than 90' (October 2025), 'a record 95' (April 2026). The only page naming members does so incidentally through seven staff profiles. All 14 RAMP ties this round were assembled one country at a time from individual World Bank press releases or the central bank's own announcement: GTM TTO KHM BGR ECU ZWE BIH ARM PRY XKX CPV LBR LBY SYC. Roughly 80 members remain unidentified; the same press-release search run year by year will keep yielding them. IMPORTANT: RAMP engagements differ in kind and each record says which. Most releases describe advice, technical assistance and training only. Seychelles is the one source found stating RAMP actually MANAGES a portfolio (US$100m from 2019), while the RAMP asset management page says the Treasury 'manages assets for all RAMP members, totaling over $30 billion' without naming a client. Do not upgrade membership or advice into management.

A second copy under /files/2024-01/ is 369 characters and fails identically. browser_round.method: Load pdf.js from cdnjs into an ordinary HTML page on the PDF's OWN origin, then getDocument(url) and walk the text layer. Where the text layer is empty the page is a scan: render that page to a canvas, replace the body with it, and screenshot. Chrome's own PDF viewer exposes no text to any reader, so navigating straight to the PDF is useless. Same origin matters - a cross-origin PDF is refused by CORS.

The bank adopted the target and open-ended asset purchases on 22 January 2013 in a joint statement; the chief cabinet secretary then said less need to revise the law. Abe repeated the threat in parliament in February 2013. Lawmakers had summoned governor Shirakawa to the Diet several times in February 2012.

auditors_four_negatives_do_not_retry.CUB: CONFIRMED STRUCTURAL BLANK. Decreto-Ley No. 361 (Del Banco Central de Cuba) has a heading 'De la certificacion de los estados financieros del Banco Central de Cuba' whose text is: the financial statements of the Banco Central de Cuba are verified by the INTERNAL auditor. The same body of law requires commercial financial institutions to be certified by civil service companies expressly authorised by the Contralor General to practise independent audit, and gives the BCC the job of selecting among those firms for OTHER institutions - so the contrast is deliberate in the statute. The BCC's own statements are not externally audited. juriscuba.com is robots-disallowed to WebFetch; cuba.vlex.com and the search result text both carry the wording. Do not retry Cuba.

Article 22 of the Monetary and Banking Law (1972) makes the Supervisory Board responsible for auditing the accounts and commitments of Bank Markazi Iran, auditing the annual balance sheet, and certifying the summary of accounts for publication. The Supervisory Board is an organ of the bank under its own statute - the MACAO PRECEDENT applies, where the AMCM's own Comissao de Fiscalizacao was not promoted to an external auditor. The Supreme Audit Court (Divan Mohasebat, constitutional articles 54-55) does audit state bodies, but a Journal of Money and Economy article records that its supervision of the Central Bank is contested, that a Guardian Council interpretation is in play, and that in practice the Court of Accounts only reviews statements already audited by audit authorities. So there is no clean statutory external auditor to name. Do not file the Supervisory Board.

The 1999 US State Department Country Commercial Guide for Eritrea states: 'In turn an independent local accounting firm audits the Central Bank of Eritrea.' It names no firm, and the next sentence only says the statements comply with international standards. Separately the Eritrean government news site shabait.com, writing about the Office of the Auditor General, says the Audit Service Corporation - semi-autonomous under the Auditor General's general supervision - audits all public enterprises and some government activities 'such as accounts of banks' and the National Insurance Corporation of Eritrea. added: TTO: Rambarran named the five largest foreign-exchange users by sector at the bank's own Monetary Policy Forum on 4 December 2015 and said the country was in recession. Named companies complained to finance minister Colm Imbert and threatened suit; the Chamber of Industry and Commerce said he had betrayed business confidence; he was accused of breaching section 56 of the Central Bank Act 1964 and section 8 of the Financial Institutions Act 2008. Summoned to Imbert on 22 December and handed a bank press release dated 8 December recording the sectors' reaction. On 24 December 2015 the Acting President revoked his appointment on Cabinet's advice, two and a half years into a five-year term from July 2012. Deputy governor Alvin Hilaire replaced him. Rampersad J held the termination unlawful and unconstitutional in June 2022 and ordered the bank to compute what was owed to July 2017; the State appealed; the case reached the Privy Council. PRIMARY SOURCE IS THE JCPC CASE SUMMARY, jcpc.uk/cases/jcpc-2025-0084 - final appellate courts publish free case summaries for small jurisdictions and they state facts plainly. Note a date conflict in the press: Newsday says 23 December, the JCPC and Trinidad Express say 24 December. Filed as 24 December on the court's authority.

ECU: article 303 of the constitution published in Registro Oficial 449 on 20 October 2008 makes the drafting of monetary, credit, exchange and financial policy the exclusive power of the Executive, instrumented through the Central Bank. The 1998 constitution had granted independence; this took it away. The monetary board became a five-member board appointed by the president and confirmed by Congress. Source is the University of Chicago monetary and fiscal history of Ecuador (Cueva and Diaz), whose timeline lists '2008 Suppression of central bank independence'; the BCE's own funciones page states its role in article 303's words, which is the corroboration. STILL IN FORCE, so no end date - file as the standing arrangement and say so in the summary.

UGA: Auditor General John Muwanga's special audit of the closure of seven commercial banks 1993-2017 went to the Speaker on 27 August 2018, requested by the committee chairman on 28 November 2017, and the bank had tried to stop it. Public hearings late 2018 into 2019 before the committee on commissions, statutory authorities and state enterprises, chaired by Abdu Katuntu, with governor Mutebile and deputy Kasekende giving evidence; sent away 1 November 2018 for arriving without documents; security officers put on oath that month. Mutebile said on 12 November the seven banks were resolved largely for insolvency, denied delegating power to agree the Global Trust Bank sale to DFCU, and said liquidation reports were kept from him by junior staff. Report finalised February 2019 recommending individual accountability; demands for action later stalled. NOTE the existing UGA corruption case already rests on the same Auditor General report - the new record is the parliamentary inquiry, a different thing, and the writeup was written to keep them distinct rather than repeat.

MUS: Bheenick governor from February 2007; first term unrenewed February 2010 during an abuse-of-power investigation, cleared and reinstated 21 May 2010, further term 2013. Days after the December 2014 election he received a letter from the secretary of the President of the Republic terminating his contract with immediate effect, confirmed by him to Reuters on 27 December 2014, saying he would consult lawyers on whether the new government had the constitutional right to sack the governor. No reason made clear. Basant Roi took over 30 December 2014. Bheenick later sued for Rs 270 million after settlement talks failed, saying he was paid a nominal Rs 10 a month over 91 months; the bank's deputy secretary confirmed about Rs 51.6 million outstanding. The bank's own past-governors page corroborates the December 2014 end date.

PER second record, closing the lead named in the round 40 handoff: law 32251 published 19 January 2025, following a Constitutional Court ruling, requires the full national coat of arms, 'Republica del Peru' and the motto 'Firme y feliz por la union' on all coins and notes. BCRP official Abraham de la Melena said the bank was not consulted in drafting or approving it. The bank's technical objections: the full arms shrink the central part of a coin's obverse, hurting striking and public recognition of security features; fitting the motto means removing or shrinking the issuing bank's own name; on notes the arms cannot go on the obverse without disturbing watermarks and fluorescent zones; coin-handling machines nationwide would need recalibration; two versions of one denomination would confuse users and help counterfeiters; redesign, tender, printing and distribution 14-15 months at high cost. Velarde: the bank will comply but it 'introduces costs', and the arms predate the bank's own 102 years. Bills 10738 and 10769 cleared the constitution committee and in March 2026 Congress approved making the arms and motto conditional on the BCRP board's approval, framed as preserving its technical and operational autonomy.

JAM: Minister of Finance terminated governor Derick Latibeaudiere's services Friday 30 October 2009 after thirteen years. PM Bruce Golding told the House the terms were 'unacceptable, embarrassing and repugnant': basic salary from 11,226,271 rising with public-sector increases plus incremental and performance adjustments to 14,545,000 by dismissal day, inside a package reported about 38 million a year, more than the Fed chairman. Set against nurses' unmet reclassification demand. Latibeaudiere wrote to the minister that day invoking pacta sunt servanda. He was lead IMF standby negotiator and in the talks until two hours before. S&P downgraded the sovereign the next day; Golding called it knee-jerk. National Workers Union questioned the legality and said he should have been consulted. The Economist reported talk of a policy disagreement with the finance minister. Wynter took over 1 December 2009. PRIMARY SOURCE IS THE PARLIAMENT OF JAMAICA HOUSE MINUTES PDF on japarliament.gov.jm carrying Golding's statement in full. PARLIAMENTARY MINUTES ARE AN UNDERUSED VEIN FOR THIS ROW - free, primary, and they state grounds the press only paraphrases.

Surinamese Bankers' Association said on 3 February 2020 the bank had misled them for months with incorrect and incomplete information about the reserve and named the then governor mainly responsible for the disappearance of over $100m from a $426m reserve. Opposition demanded Bouterse explain in Parliament and said the government should resign otherwise, accusing it of servicing foreign debt with the money; the Vice President said the government had agreements with the banks and the central bank had not kept its end. Van Trikt removed January 2020, resigned 4 February. 22 March 2020 law temporarily blocked FX transactions. Kind 'reserves taken'. Source state.gov 2020 Investment Climate Statement. NOTE van Trikt's prosecution is ALREADY a SUR corruption case - this record is deliberately the government's side, and the writeup keeps them apart. NIC, the weakest of the four, reasoning recorded on purpose: Ley de Administracion del Sistema Monetario y Financiero (law 1232), sent to the Assembly 19 December 2024, to committee 23 December during the legislative recess, approved 26 December, published in La Gaceta 30 December. Repealed the Organic Law of the Central Bank of Nicaragua AND the Superintendency law, merged the two formerly independent institutions under one statute and one common board chaired by BCN president Ovidio Reyes, abolished the Superintendency's own board, and gave Reyes coordination of the Financial Analysis Unit and the deposit fund. Article 24 obliges every person resident or domiciled in Nicaragua, national or foreign, to supply the bank and Superintendency with whatever information they request. THE HEDGE IS THE POINT: the law's own text says the institutions retain organic, functional, administrative, financial and budgetary autonomy and their institutional specialisation; Divergentes says it eliminates their autonomy and gives plenipotentiary powers to Reyes and the Executive. The bank did not object and its president GAINED power. Filed on the Ecuador precedent set in round 41 - the statute governing the bank rewritten by the Executive without consultation - with both readings in the record and the writeup. IF A LATER ROUND DECIDES A BANK THAT GAINS POWER HAS NOT BEEN MOVED AGAINST, REVISIT THIS RECORD ON THE REASONING; do not quietly drop it.
